subject: Is this a bug with geom step?

messages.author: a0e82b98c8b5b862
messages.subject: Is this a bug with geom step?
parts:
ggplot2 group,

I am trying to create a step function plot using ggplot2.  I can create the plot just fine but an issue arises when I try to adjust the line thickness since it can be a little hard to see the lines.  I am attaching a small data set to reproduce the example.  I try to use the base R plot option "lwd" to adjust the thickness of the line.  However, when I add lwd to qplot it changes the plotting character for the points on the graph (i.e., the solid points turn to triangles).  Some simple code is given below to reproduce this potential bug:

##This gives solid dots by default
qplot(heights,prob,data = surv.dat,geom = "step",group = thick, color = thick) + geom_point(aes(x = heights,y=prob))

##Adding lwd to qplot changes plotting characters to triangles
qplot(heights,prob,data = surv.dat,geom = "step",group = thick, color = thick,lwd = 2) + geom_point(aes(x = heights,y=prob))

I imagine this is more me not fully understanding the usage of geom_step, in which case I thank you for any corrections ahead of time.  But just in case this is a bug I figure I would send out a reproducible example.  Thank you all for your help.

Best,
Brian

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Is this a bug with geom step?
parts:
Hi Brian,
Use the ggplot aesthetics. To change the thickness of the line, use size =

= thick, size = I(2)) + geom_point(aes(x = heights,y=prob))

As an aside, I strongly recommend switching to the ggplot syntax
instead of qplot. qplot tries to simplify, but ultimately I think the
ggplot syntax is actually easier to use (that is a subjective claim of
course, and your experience may differ). A ggplot version is

ggplot(surv.dat, aes(x=heights, y=prob, colour = factor(thick))) +
geom_point(size=4) +
geom_step(size=2)

Best,
Ista

While I agree with Ista that learning the ggplot syntax is good in the
long run, the code you had should work. I imagine that the problem is
you have a pre 1.5.1 version of plyr; there was a bug in 1.5 that could
cause an error like this (mismatch of aesthetics when using the
non-canonical forms of the names of aesthetics).
